verses.text: About the Ammonites. This is what the LORD says: "Does Israel have no sons? Does it have no heir? Then why has Molech taken over the land of Gad, and why do his people live in its towns?

So look, the days are coming," says the LORD, "when I will sound the battle cry against Rabbah of the Ammonites. It will become a heap of ruins, and its surrounding villages will be burned down. Then Israel will drive out those who drove them out," says the LORD.

"Wail, Heshbon, because Ai is destroyed! Cry out, you people of Rabbah! Put on sackcloth and mourn. Run here and there inside the walls, because Molech will go into exile, along with his priests and officials.
Why do you boast about your valleys, your fruitful valleys, you unfaithful daughter? You trusted in your riches and said, 'Who would dare attack me?'
Look, I will bring terror on you from everyone around you," says the Lord GOD of Armies. "Each of you will be driven away, and no one will gather those who run away.
But later I will bring the Ammonites back from captivity," says the LORD.
About Edom. This is what the LORD of Armies says: "Is there no more wisdom in Teman? Have the wise run out of good advice? Has their wisdom disappeared?
Turn and run! Hide in deep caves, you people of Dedan! For I will bring disaster on Esau's descendants when I come to punish them.
If grape pickers came to you, wouldn't they leave a few grapes behind? If thieves came at night, wouldn't they steal only as much as they wanted?
But I will strip Esau's descendants bare. I will uncover their hiding places, and they will not be able to hide. Their children, relatives, and neighbors will be destroyed, and they will be no more.
Leave your orphans behind, and I will keep them alive. Your widows can trust in me."
This is what the LORD says: "If those who did not deserve to drink from the cup of punishment must drink it, why should you go unpunished? You will not go unpunished. You must drink it.
For I have sworn by myself," says the LORD, "that Bozrah will become an object of horror, disgrace, ruin, and cursing. All its towns will be ruins forever."
I have heard a message from the LORD. A messenger has been sent to the nations to say: "Gather together and attack her! Get ready for battle!"
"Look, I will make you small among the nations, looked down on by everyone.

The terror you inspire and the pride of your heart have fooled you. You live in the clefts of the rocks and hold the high places of the hills. But even if you build your nest as high as an eagle's, I will bring you down from there," says the LORD.
"Edom will become an object of horror. Everyone who passes by will be shocked and will gasp at all its wounds.
Like Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighboring towns when they were destroyed," says the LORD, "no one will live there. No human being will stay there.

Look, like a lion coming up from the thick bushes along the Jordan to a rich pasture, I will suddenly chase Edom from its land. I will appoint over it whomever I choose. For who is like me? Who can challenge me? What shepherd can stand against me?"
So listen to the plan the LORD has made against Edom, and what he intends to do to the people of Teman: Even the youngest of the flock will be dragged away. He will completely destroy their pasture.
At the sound of their fall the earth will shake. Their cries will be heard as far as the Red Sea.
Look, an enemy will rise up and swoop down like an eagle, spreading its wings over Bozrah. On that day the hearts of Edom's warriors will be like the heart of a woman in labor.
About Damascus. "Hamath and Arpad are put to shame, because they have heard bad news. They melt with fear, troubled like the restless sea that cannot be calm.
Damascus has become weak. She turns to run away, and panic grips her. Pain and suffering have seized her like a woman in labor.
How sad that the famous city has not been abandoned, the town that gave me joy!
So her young men will fall in her streets, and all her soldiers will be silenced on that day," says the LORD of Armies.
"I will set fire to the walls of Damascus, and it will burn down the palaces of Ben-Hadad."
About Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon attacked. This is what the LORD says: "Get up and attack Kedar! Destroy the people of the east!
Their tents and flocks will be taken. Their tent curtains, all their goods, and their camels will be carried off. People will shout to them, 'Terror on every side!'
Run away! Escape far away! Hide in deep caves, you people of Hazor," says the LORD. "For Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has made a plan against you. He has decided to attack you.
Get up and attack a nation that is at ease and feels secure," says the LORD. "It has no gates or bars. Its people live alone.

Their camels will be taken as loot, and their many cattle as plunder. I will scatter to every wind those who cut the corners of their hair, and I will bring disaster on them from every side," says the LORD.
"Hazor will become a home for jackals, a ruin forever. No one will live there. No human being will stay there."
This is the LORD's message that came to Jeremiah the prophet about Elam, early in the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah:
"This is what the LORD of Armies says: Look, I will break the bow of Elam, the source of their strength.
I will bring the four winds from the four corners of the sky against Elam. I will scatter its people to all these winds. There will not be a nation where Elam's exiles do not go.

I will make Elam terrified before their enemies, before those who want to kill them. I will bring disaster on them, my fierce anger," says the LORD. "I will chase them with the sword until I have destroyed them.
I will set my throne in Elam and destroy its king and officials," says the LORD.
"But in the days to come I will bring Elam back from captivity," says the LORD.
